'''Boschwitz:''' {{legend0|#ffb2b2|40–50%}} {{legend0|#e27f7f|50–60%}} {{legend0|#d75d5d|60–70%}} | title = U.S. Senator | before_election = [[Rudy Boschwitz]] | before_party = Independent-Republicans of Minnesota | after_election = [[Paul Wellstone]] | after_party = Minnesota Democratic–Farmer–Labor Party }} {{Elections in Minnesota}} The '''1990 United States Senate election in Minnesota''' was held on November 6, 1990. Incumbent Republican U.S. Senator [[Rudy Boschwitz]] was defeated by Democratic challenger [[Paul Wellstone]] in a tight race. Widely considered an underdog and outspent by a 7-to-1 margin, Wellstone was the only candidate to both defeat an incumbent senator and flip a seat in the [[1990 United States Senate elections|1990 election cycle]]; he gained national attention after his [[Upset (competition)|upset victory]]. The race was also notable as the first in the history of the U.S. Senate where both major-party candidates were [[Jews|Jewish]]. Wellstone was re-elected in [[1996 United States Senate election in Minnesota|1996]] in a rematch with Boschwitz. == Background == {{Main|1984 United States Senate election in Minnesota}} In 1984, despite Democrat [[Walter Mondale]]'s narrow victory in the state in the [[1984 United States presidential election|concurrent presidential election]],{{Cite news |last=Raines |first=Howell |date=November 7, 1984 |title=Reagan Wins By a Landslide, Sweeping at Least 48 States; G.O.P. Gains Strength in House |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1984/11/07/politics/reagan-wins-by-a-landslide-sweeping-at-least-48-states-gop-gains.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170825144938/http://www.nytimes.com/1984/11/07/politics/07REAG.html?pagewanted=1 |archive-date=August 25, 2017 |access-date=March 12, 2025 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}{{Cite news |last=Balz |first=Dan |date=2021-04-20 |title=Mondale lost the presidency but permanently changed the office of vice presidency |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/mondale-lost-the-presidency-but-permanently-changed-the-office-of-vice-presidency/2021/04/19/478b1a68-a17b-11eb-85fc-06664ff4489d_story.html |access-date=2025-05-26 |work=[[The Washington Post]] |language=en-US |issn=0190-8286}} Rudy Boschwitz won reelection to a second term, defeating Democratic challenger [[Joan Growe]] 58% to 41%.{{Cite web |last=Ladd |first=Thomas E. |date=May 1, 1985 |title=Statistics of the Presidential and Congressional Election of November 6, 1984 |url=https://clerk.house.gov/member_info/electionInfo/1984election.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210129075653/https://clerk.house.gov/member_info/electionInfo/1984election.pdf |archive-date=January 29, 2021 |access-date=March 11, 2025 |website=[[Clerk of the United States House of Representatives]] |page=10}}{{Cite web |title=Biden, Joseph Robinette (Joe), Jr. (1942–) |url=https://bioguideretro.congress.gov/Home/MemberDetails?memIndex=b000444 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250225204059/https://bioguideretro.congress.gov/Home/MemberDetails?memIndex=b000444 |archive-date=February 25, 2025 |access-date=March 11, 2025 |website=[[Biographical Directory of the United States Congress]]}} The election was held as part of the [[United States midterm election|midterm election cycle]] of Republican president [[George H. W. Bush]]'s term.{{Cite news |last1=Dewar |first1=Helen |last2=Yang |first2=John E. |date=November 6, 1990 |title=The Senate Incumbents Win Control Remains with Democrats |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/politics/1990/11/07/the-senate/88a317b4-abae-4a7c-9a3c-f65fe6b52b54/ |access-date=March 12, 2025 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]}} == General election == === Candidates === * [[Russell Bentley]], lumberjack and [[Legality of cannabis|marijuana legalization]] activist (Grassroots) * [[Rudy Boschwitz]], incumbent U.S. Senator since 1979 (Independent-Republican) * [[Paul Wellstone]], professor at [[Carleton College]] and nominee for [[Minnesota State Auditor]] in 1982 (DFL) === Campaign === Paul Wellstone was considered to be a longshot candidate, being outspent by a margin of 7-to-1. Wellstone used grassroots campaigning tactics, and quirky campaign ads like "Fast Paul",{{Citation |title=Paul Wellstone TV Ad "Fast Paul" |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NbmMlTsKo30 |language=en |access-date=2023-01-01}} where he spoke quickly about himself and his platform, and "Looking for Rudy",{{Citation |title=North Woods Advertising - "Looking for Rudy" - Paul Wellstone for U.S. Senate (MN) |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nfZuplTlu4M |language=en |access-date=2023-01-01}} a two minute ad where he went searching for his opponent Rudy Boschwitz throughout Minnesota. === Debates === {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center;" |+ 1990 United States Senate election in Minnesota debates |- ! scope="col" | {{abbr|No.|Number}} ! scope="col" | Date ! scope="col" | Host ! scope="col" | Moderator ! scope="col" | Link ! scope="col"| [[Republican Party (US)|Republican]] ! scope="col"| [[Democratic Party (US)|Democratic]] |- ! colspan="5" rowspan="2" |Key:
